questions.question: A company wants the most control over the security configuration of its operating systems in the cloud. Which service type should it choose?

options.why: Correct. You manage and configure the OS.
The provider manages the OS in PaaS.

questions.explanation: IaaS gives maximum control over OS-level security, with matching responsibility.

questions.question: Which Azure service helps protect applications from distributed denial of service attacks?

options.why: Advisor gives recommendations; it does not block attacks.
Arc extends management to other environments.

questions.explanation: Azure DDoS Protection mitigates volumetric and protocol attacks on Azure resources.

questions.question: Which TWO are security benefits of using PaaS instead of IaaS?

options.text: Operating system patches are applied by the provider
The customer no longer needs to manage user access
options.why: Access and identities remain the customer's responsibility.

options.text: Less infrastructure for the customer to secure

options.why: Data always remains the customer's responsibility.

questions.explanation: PaaS shifts platform patching and infrastructure security to the provider, while data and access stay with you.

questions.question: Which Azure service provides a secure score, security recommendations and threat protection for Azure, hybrid and multi-cloud resources?

options.why: Azure Monitor collects telemetry; Defender for Cloud provides security posture and threat protection.
Policy enforces rules but does not provide threat protection.

questions.explanation: Defender for Cloud combines security posture management (secure score) with workload protection.
